title: Thinking of putting up $10k to get people to stress test our prediction market API via Agents
author: Junior-City
selftext:
I built a prediction market API suite and I really want more traders/devs to use it and give us real feedback. Not “looks cool” feedback, but actually build on it, trade through it, break things, and tell us what’s annoying or missing.

Was thinking of putting up like **$10k of our own money** and running a free trading/building competition around it.

Goal is to useAI, agents, whatever you want. I mostly want a reason for good traders/builders to spend some time with the APIs in an agentic fashion and push them harder than we can internally.

Would probably reward some mix of actual trading performance + interesting strategies/builds rather than just whoever takes the most risk and gets lucky.

No entry fee or anything.

Would people actually spend a weekend / week doing this for a $10k pool?

Also curious what would make it fun enough that you’d actually participate.

comments.author: Junior-City
comments.body: Open to feedback here, curious if it's of interest just wanna validate our product :)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
a prize pool buys you volume, not the kind of feedback you are describing. people optimising for a leaderboard go looking for the edge in your scoring rules, and what you learn at the end is a great deal about your scoring rules.

the builders whose complaints are actually worth having are the ones who would use the api anyway, and those people are usually too busy to enter a competition. paying a handful of them for two days and a written writeup gets you further than ten grand spread across a field.

replies.author: Junior-City
replies.body: Makes sense, the trouble is the alignment is also not correct there either. A write up does not mean much if people are not winning; however, if we get 2-3 traders from the competition that win and stick around can be long-term meaningful.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
A prize over a short window selects for variance, not skill. Whoever sizes biggest takes it, and that person is the least likely to still be around in six months.

A longer window or risk adjusted scoring changes who wins entirely, though it also makes it much less fun to watch.

comments.author: DesertClimber
comments.body: I've seen trading competition leaderboards that are so skewed towards people going 'full port', simply going for massive gains at the expense of any real consistency.

replies.author: Junior-City
replies.body: Makes sense, yeah I think we have created this with many different prize pools roi, consistency, net pnl, and volume so hopefully folks are rewarded for diverse behaviors versus just crazy profits by punting. Let me know! The docs are here, and feel free to pm. [docs.kairos.trade](http://docs.kairos.trade) (kairos.trade) being the website.

comments.author: VisibleBee
comments.body: I would make the competition test the system, not just the agents: freeze the market and API behavior for each run, record rejected and failed orders, and score robustness alongside returns. The best result should be the one that survives replay, costs, and adversarial edge cases.

replies.author: Junior-City
replies.body: Makes sense, I'll start trying this out. I would love your feedback on the platform if you do trade prediction markets.
